chapter_title: The Fun They Had & The Road Not Taken
summary: This unit pairs Sudha Murty's biographical memoir 'How I Taught My Grandmother to Read' with Subramania Bharati's nationalist poem 'Bharat Our Land'. The prose recounts the determination of Krishtakka, a 62-year-old illiterate village woman, who learns the Kannada alphabet from her 12-year-old granddaughter after experiencing intense helplessness when she cannot read her favorite serialized novel 'Kashi Yatre'. The poem celebrates India's majestic physical geography, spiritual heritage, intellectual traditions, and egalitarian societal ideals.

hotspots.title: Phase 1: Dependence
hotspots.description: Krishtakka relied on her 12-year-old granddaughter to read aloud weekly instalments of Kashi Yatre.

hotspots.title: Phase 3: The Vow
hotspots.description: Vowed at age 62 to learn the Kannada alphabet by Saraswati Pooja during Dussehra.

hotspots.title: Phase 5: Self-Reliance
hotspots.description: Read Kashi Yatre fluently and touched her granddaughter's feet as a Guru.

key_takeaways: Age is no bar for learning when supported by determination and passion.
Literacy bestows personal independence, self-respect, and dignity.
Respect for a teacher (Guru) transcends age boundaries.
